speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
title: O Be Wise
session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: President D. Todd Christofferson spoke about “O Be Wise”.

quotes.text: President Gordon B. Hinckley, in addressing this subject over 20 years ago, mentioned a story about former United States President Calvin Coolidge, known as a man of few words. As Coolidge returned home from church one Sunday, his wife asked him what the preacher spoke about. He replied, “Sin.”
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: The smartphone has transformed gambling from an occasional activity requiring a trip to a casino, racetrack, or lottery kiosk into an activity available continuously, privately, and almost anywhere. This has led to an explosion in gambling. Worldwide surveys spanning multiple years indicate that 46 percent of adults gambled in the last 12 months—that is about 2.3 billion people. The global gambling industry generated estimated revenues of $758 billion in 2025. Of course, the industry’s revenue is the gambler’s loss. Simply put, the industry’s entire business model is built on its customers losing money.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Youth and young adults are disproportionately affected. For this demographic, impulsivity and peer influence are compounded by early exposure, easy online access, and intense marketing. Widespread social acceptance only adds to the enticement. Sports betting is especially rampant among teenagers and young adults. It easily becomes consuming and often compulsive. It robs time from studies, relationships, and career development. It crowds out things of value and in their place fosters greed.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Surveys reveal that people know that in gambling the odds are stacked against them, and the house always wins—they just don’t think it will win against them personally. But the central risk of gambling is not merely that customers lose money on individual wagers. The larger concern is that continuous, mobile access can transform occasional entertainment into repeated behavior that displaces saving, increases debt, and creates far-reaching family and social costs. I have to agree with George Washington when he said of gambling, “It is the child of avarice—the brother of inequity—and father of mischief” (although calling it “mischief” may be too mild).
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Perhaps you think your character and your commitment to divine covenants are sufficiently strong that, for you, wagers would never become more than occasional, casual fun. Maybe. But whether you are right about that or not, have you considered how your example might affect others?
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: If your moral standing is secure, then undoubtedly there are others who look to you as a guide for upright living. That would certainly be true for your children but also others that you may or may not know who are watching and learning from what they see in you. They may be newer or weaker in the faith. A little gambling that seemingly has only a minor impact in your life may be more costly to them if they take license from your example.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: “For if any man see thee which hast knowledge [of the gospel] sit at meat in the idol’s temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: President Oaks clearly stated the moral case against gambling some years ago in these words: “What does gambling do to its participants? The attitude of taking something from someone else in order to enhance our own position—[which is] the essence of gambling—leads us away from the giving path of Christ and toward the taking path of the adversary. The act of taking or trying to take something from someone else without giving value in return is destructive of spiritual sensitivities.”
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference
